messages:
sam: quick question — we have a few customers asking about telemetry headers across SDKs. main points: what exactly goes in the user-agent, how do we propagate tracing (`traceparent`), and what's the supported way to disable client metrics?

alex: short answers first: UA is lightweight (sdk/version + runtime), tracing follows W3C `traceparent`/`tracestate`, and each SDK has a `telemetry: false` config + env var. details below.

priya: can we standardize header names? customers see a mix of `User-Agent`, `X-Redwood-User-Agent`, and sometimes our internal `x-rw-trace`. makes integrations messy.

alex: yeah — prefer the standard `User-Agent` for client identifier. we add an opt-in `X-Redwood-User-Agent` for extra metadata (model hints, infra) but it's only added when `telemetry.enabled = true`. otherwise `User-Agent` contains `redwood-sdk/<version>` and runtime (e.g., `node`/`python`).

matt_r: example JS UA: `User-Agent: redwood-sdk-js/1.4.2 node/20.1.0` — no user emails/IDs. don't include app-specific tokens.

jenna: python example: `User-Agent: redwood-sdk-py/0.9.0 python/3.11`

sam: good. tracing: customers want their trace injected into our pipeline. do we accept `traceparent` and `tracestate`? what about our legacy `x-rw-trace`?

alex: yes accept W3C `traceparent` + `tracestate` (highest priority). if both W3C headers are absent but `x-rw-trace` present, convert to a `traceparent`-compatible form and propagate internally. document that `x-rw-trace` is legacy and will be deprioritized.

priya: important for streaming: websockets/sse handshakes only allow headers at connection time. if a customer needs tracing per-chunk, they must include trace id in the first handshake or send a chunk-level metadata field (we support JSON chunk prefix like { "trace_id": "..." }). mention in guides.

matt_r: streaming gotcha: retries must NOT replay partial streams. our client will only retry non-streaming requests automatically. streaming calls return a stream object and any retry must be done by the user (with idempotency token). add a note in SDK docs.

jenna: how to disable client metrics entirely? we have env var examples for each SDK, right?

alex: yes — per-SDK options: JS: `new Redwood({ telemetry: { enabled: false }})` or set `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=false` env var. Py: `client = Redwood(telemetry_enabled=False)` or `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=false`. Go: `redwood.NewClient(redwood.Config{TelemetryEnabled: false})` or `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=false`.

sam: do metrics disabling also stop UA header? I think UA still sent but trimmed to `redwood-sdk/<ver>` with no extra fields. need to be explicit.

alex: correct. even when telemetry disabled we still send a minimal `User-Agent` for routing/versioning. we never include any PII in headers. full telemetry (runtime details, model tags) is only sent if enabled.

observability-bot: FYI — logging note: when telemetry is disabled, we still emit a small internal request id header `X-Request-ID` for debug, but it's not linked to user-provided identifiers.

priya: also add guidance for proxies and load balancers: make sure they forward `traceparent` and `User-Agent`. some infra strips unknown headers.

sam: actionable items: 1) add small section in each SDK README with exact header formats + disable examples, 2) update streaming doc with handshake vs per-chunk tracing, 3) announce legacy `x-rw-trace` deprecation timeline.

jenna: I'll own the SDK READMEs (py/js/go samples). tagging @matt_r for streaming doc changes.

matt_r: got it. I'll add retry/streaming note and a code sample showing explicit retry with idempotency token.

sam: thanks — if anyone has quick code snippets for the README I can paste in.

alex: paste these minimal bits: JS: ```js const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, telemetry: { enabled: false } }); // UA: redwood-sdk-js/1.4.2 node/20.1.0 ``` Py: ```py client = Redwood(api_key=os.getenv('RW_KEY'), telemetry_enabled=False) # UA: redwood-sdk-py/0.9.0 python/3.11 ``` Go: ```go cfg := redwood.DefaultConfig() cfg.TelemetryEnabled = false client := redwood.NewClient(cfg) // UA: redwood-sdk-go/0.3.1 go/1.20 ```

priya: perfect. I also suggest a short FAQ line: "How to ensure no telemetry leaves my VPC?" -> Use Private deployment + telemetry disabled in SDK; note that minimal routing UA and X-Request-ID may still be present.

sam: awesome. I'll file a small GH issue to track the README updates and the deprecation note for `x-rw-trace`. thanks folks :thumbsup:

jenna: thanks! :rocket:
